bio:
Tree: Giovanni P. Dibiasi (b. 1829) + Rosa Siconolfi (b. 1840); his parents Domenico Di Biase (b. 1789) + Angela Carrozzino. FS tree G4YR-BXY: Giovanni Pasquale DiBiasi (b. c.1829) and Rosa Siconolfi (b. 1839) 'born Lucera, Foggia', with zero sources. Their children Domenico Antonio (1856) and Maria Antonia (1870) were born in Guardia. The same FS profiles list children born in 1891 and 1894, when Rosa would have been 52-55 - mis-attachments. Round 1 concluded the Lucera thumbnail (on Domenico Di Biase in the Ancestry tree) is probably someone else's record: Guardia's records are at AS Avellino, while Lucera holds a branch archive for Foggia-province records and Di Biase is a common Capitanata surname. Round 2: remove Lucera. Round 3: still speculative/unsourced.

The FamilySearch tree attaches four children to Giovanni Pasquale and Rosa Siconolfi: Domenico Antonio (1856), Maria Antonia (1870), Joseph (b. 18 Apr 1891) and Vincenzo 'James' (b. 2 Mar 1894). It cites no sources for him ([R4-S1]). The two youngest cannot be theirs, because Rosa would have been 52–55. The April 1940 census shows Joseph DiBiasi (47, born Italy) and James DiBiasi (45, born Italy) as neighbours at 1015 Bunker Hill Street ([R4-S2]). Three doors from the Petriello house, at 1022, lived a widowed Vincenzo DiBiasi, aged 74 (born c.1866), with his son Michael ([R4-S3]). That Vincenzo is a more plausible father for Joseph and James, and possibly a younger son of Giovanni Pasquale himself, which would make him Maria Antonia's brother.
